content.value_statement: Architecture decisions can become unclear when requirements, team skills, and future growth compete. This skill compares suitable patterns and helps document a clear, reasoned decision.
actual_capabilities: Matches layered, clean, hexagonal, event-driven, and CQRS patterns to common project needs.
Uses project and team size as inputs for initial architecture recommendations.
Provides feature-based and layer-based directory structure examples.
Guides trade-off analysis across complexity, scalability, and team familiarity.
Supplies validation criteria for module boundaries, dependencies, testing, and growth.
limitations: Does not inspect an existing codebase or measure its operational requirements.
Does not produce implementation code, deployment configurations, or cost estimates.
Recommendations are general guidance and require validation against product constraints.
Does not replace review by experienced engineers and stakeholders.

use_cases.title: Plan a new product foundation
use_cases.description: Compare a modular monolith with other patterns before a small product team begins implementation.

use_cases.title: Document an architecture decision
use_cases.description: Record options, trade-offs, and consequences for a system change in a consistent format.

use_cases.title: Choose a project structure
use_cases.description: Select a feature-based or layer-based directory layout that fits a growing application.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a simple starting pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: I am building a small CRUD web application with three developers. Recommend an architecture pattern and explain why.

prompt_templates.title: Compare two approaches
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare a modular monolith and microservices for an e-commerce platform with a team of eight developers. Include trade-offs.

prompt_templates.title: Create a decision record
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an architecture decision record for choosing clean architecture in a long-lived billing service. Include context, options, trade-offs, decision, and consequences.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a proposed design
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this proposed event-driven architecture against team skills, testing needs, module boundaries, scalability, and operational complexity: [describe the system].

output_examples.input: Recommend an architecture for a medium-sized application with complex business rules.
output: Reason: It separates business rules from framework and database details.
Trade-off: It requires more initial structure and discipline than a layered design.

output_examples.input: Help document a choice between a modular monolith and microservices.
output: Context: The team needs independent modules but has limited operational capacity.
Decision: Start with a modular monolith.
Consequence: Define strict module boundaries and reconsider service extraction when operational needs justify it.

best_practices: Start with the simplest design that meets current requirements.
Document assumptions, alternatives, and consequences with every major decision.
Validate the proposed design with developers who will build and maintain it.
anti_patterns: Choosing microservices only because they are popular.
Copying an architecture without considering team skills and operational capacity.
Treating an architecture decision as permanent when requirements change.

faq.question: What architecture patterns does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers layered, clean, hexagonal, event-driven, CQRS, modular monolith, and microservice approaches.

faq.question: Can it choose an architecture without project details?
faq.answer: It can provide a starting point, but project size, requirements, team skills, and constraints improve recommendations.

faq.question: Does it recommend microservices by default?
faq.answer: No. It recommends starting simply and using microservices only when the benefits justify their added complexity.

faq.question: Can it help create an architecture decision record?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a template for documenting context, options, trade-offs, decisions, and consequences.

faq.question: Does it generate a directory structure?
faq.answer: It provides feature-based and layer-based examples that you can adapt to your application.

faq.question: Does it replace an architecture review?
faq.answer: No. Use its guidance as input to an engineering review with relevant stakeholders.
